## Apply a power, then divide {#worked}

Apply the outside power to every factor in the brackets. Then divide coefficients and subtract indices of like bases.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$\dfrac{(6a^3)^2}{2a^2}$

::: {.fragment}

[Square both factors.]{.annotation}

$=\dfrac{36a^6}{2a^2}$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Divide and subtract indices.]{.annotation}

$=\dfrac{36}{2}a^{6-2}=18a^4$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$\dfrac{(6a^3)^2}{4a^2}$

The denominator coefficient doubles. Predict the new coefficient, then simplify on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$=\dfrac{36a^6}{4a^2}$

$=\dfrac{36}{4}a^{6-2}=9a^4$

:::
